guarantees.claim: hw2reg.status.sha3_idle.d asserts when sha3_fsm equals sha3_pkg::StIdle, deasserts otherwise.
hw2reg.status.sha3_absorb.d asserts when sha3_fsm equals sha3_pkg::StAbsorb, deasserts otherwise.
hw2reg.status.sha3_squeeze.d asserts when sha3_fsm equals sha3_pkg::StSqueeze, deasserts otherwise.
hw2reg.status.fifo_depth.d[MsgFifoDepthW-1:0] is driven by msgfifo_depth; any upper bits of hw2reg.status.fifo_depth.d beyond MsgFifoDepthW are tied to 0.
engine_stable is asserted exclusively when sha3_fsm equals sha3_pkg::StIdle.
hw2reg.cfg_regwen.d is driven by engine_stable, i.e., high only when sha3_fsm is in StIdle.

assumptions.claim: MsgFifoDepthW parameter is exactly the bit width of msgfifo_depth. The chunk directly assigns lower bits and ties off extra upper bits on the status register side, but it does not protect against msgfifo_depth being wider than MsgFifoDepthW (truncation) or narrower (zero‑filled, which is safe).
assumptions.risk: If MsgFifoDepthW < $bits(msgfifo_depth), the high bits of the actual depth are lost, resulting in a falsely low depth reading and possible FIFO overflow or stall misjudgment.

uncertain_points.claim: cfg_regwen.d is a combinational decode of sha3_fsm. A configuration register write that straddles a state transition away from StIdle may see the enable glitch or deassert mid‑cycle, potentially blocking a legitimate update or allowing a write just as the engine leaves idle.
uncertain_points.cond: sha3_fsm transitions near a configuration write cycle
uncertain_points.risk: Unauthorized configuration register write while engine is not idle, or denial of a valid update, violating the SEC_CM requirement that CFG_SHADOWED.CONFIG.REGWEN gates writes only when idle.

uncertain_points.claim: No width checking or assertion guards the assignment hw2reg.status.fifo_depth.d[MsgFifoDepthW-1:0] = msgfifo_depth. If msgfifo_depth is wider than MsgFifoDepthW, the upper bits are silently truncated.
uncertain_points.risk: Software reads a truncated depth value, potentially misjudging FIFO empty/full/almost status, which could lead to data loss or stalling the pipeline incorrectly.
